title: Cluster pressure snapshot & on-call notes (node pressure / CNI flaps)
body:
Summary:

Brief notes from the 2025-11-01 incident window where a subset of clusters in us-west-2 experienced elevated node pressure resulting in pods stuck Pending and a few control-plane errors (etcd leader election spikes). Symptoms looked like memory pressure on several AWS m5a nodes plus transient CNI flaps that caused kube-proxy endpoints to go missing for small windows.

This doc is a working on-call record + runbook draft. It contains commands run, quick mitigations, hypotheses, and action items for a formal postmortem. Use this to iterate the runbook and add links to preserved logs/metrics.

Immediate detection and paging:
- 2025-11-01T02:17Z: Alert NodeMemoryPressureCount > 3 in cluster-prod-usw2, pager triggered (P1).
- 02:19Z: Multiple pods in namespace customer-serving reported Pending with message: "0/120 nodes are available: 50 Insufficient memory, 70 node(s) had taint xyz:NoSchedule"
- 02:21Z: etcd leader election count spike observed on control-plane-prom (graph in linked artifacts).

Quick timeline (observed)
- 02:15Z: Autoscaler activity increased (scale-out events started, some throttled because of instance quota).
- 02:16Z: First NodeMemoryPressure alert fired for node i-0a1b2c3d.
- 02:18Z: CNI (calico) pod on node i-0a1b2c3d restarted unexpectedly; logs show BPF program error: "RTNETLINK answers: File exists" repeatedly for ~30s.
- 02:20Z: kube-proxy endpoints for kube-system/kube-dns temporarily disappeared on 3 nodes; DNS failures and liveness probes start to fail for short windows.
- 02:21Z: control-plane etcd leader elections + increased disk IO on etcd nodes (pattern consistent with heavy GC from a monitoring job).
- 02:30Z: Mitigation steps applied (see below); cluster stabilized by 02:44Z.

Commands used during triage (copyable):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl describe node i-0a1b2c3d | sed -n '1,120p'
- kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep -E 'Pending|CrashLoopBackOff'
- journalctl -u kubelet -o cat | tail -n 200 on affected node (via bastion)
- kubectl logs -n kube-system calico-node-xxxxx --tail=200
- kubectl get endpoints kube-dns -n kube-system -o yaml

Observed partial outputs (redacted):
- describe node i-0a1b2c3d: Allocatable memory 62Gi, Allocated 59.7Gi, Allocatable ephemeral-storage reduced (ephemeral-storage pressure events observed).
- calico logs: "ERR: BPF program install failed: RTNETLINK answers: File exists" followed by repeated IPtables/ebtables sync warnings.
- kubelet: "eviction manager: attempting to reclaim memory" then "eviction threshold breached, evicting best-effort pods".

What we tried (chronological) and outcome:
1) Increased cluster autoscaler target temporarily (02:22Z) to add more nodes; blocked by EC2 quota for a short time. Outcome: partial nodes added at 02:28Z, helped relieve scheduling pressure.
2) Cordoned the most-pressured nodes (02:24Z) and drained non-critical pods to free memory. Outcome: Freed ~6-8Gi per node but CNI flaps meant some system pods restarted and re-scheduled.
3) Restarted calico-node on 3 problematic nodes via kubectl delete pod -n kube-system (02:27Z). Outcome: calico restarted cleanly on 2 nodes; one node showed same BPF error and required full node reboot (later).
4) Applied temporary kubelet eviction threshold increase on 4 nodes (02:30Z) to avoid rapid pod churn; outcome: smoothed evictions, but this is a short-term band-aid.
5) On control plane, verified etcd snapshots and disk IO; rotated a monitoring job (heavy prometheus scrape) that was running a head-of-line collection every 5s for a single endpoint (02:33Z). Outcome: etcd leader election spike subsided after job tweak.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- Primary: Burst of background batch jobs (internal benchmarking/ingest) caused memory and ephemeral-storage pressure concurrently while autoscaler couldn't immediately add nodes because of quota; this pushed kubelet eviction thresholds and triggered CNI restarts on nodes with high kernel BPF table counts.
- Secondary: A recent calico upgrade (rolling) changed BPF map cleanup behavior; in combination with heavy pod churn, BPF map re-installation failed with "File exists" and caused packet drops while endpoints were reprogrammed.
- Tertiary: etcd leader election noise was caused by a monitoring job occasionally hammering control-plane endpoints, exacerbating scheduling when kube-controller-manager couldn't reconcile fast enough.

Runbook draft: "Node memory pressure + CNI flaps" (for on-call)
- Detection: NodeMemoryPressure > 2 in 5min AND >5 pods Pending with Insufficient memory.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Identify top-3 nodes by memory pressure: kubectl top nodes --no-headers | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 5
  2) Check system pods on those nodes: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
  3) If calico or kube-proxy on node in CrashLoop/Restarting -> kubectl logs and try kubectl delete pod to force restart.
  4) If BPF errors in calico logs (RTNETLINK/File exists) -> avoid mass calico pod restarts across cluster; restart only on affected node and monitor.
  5) If autoscaler not scaling: check cloud provider quota and CA logs (kubectl -n cluster-autoscaler logs). If quota is the blocker, open internal infra-requests (link template in linked_artifacts).
  6) If scheduling blocked due to taints, check if taints are stale (e.g., from previous maintenance). Remove with: kubectl taint nodes <node> key:NoSchedule- with caution.
  7) If etcd leader election spikes: reduce scrape frequency of noisy monitoring jobs (prometheus rules), check disk IO on etcd nodes, and consider locking heavy jobs backoff for 10m.
  8) Escalation: If >30m unresolved and customer latency SLOs impacted, escalate to SRE lead (Diego Alvarez) and open a paged bridge.

Short-term mitigation notes and why we chose them:
- Prefer node cordon + selective drain over mass restarts because mass calico restarts across many nodes can create a larger outage window for networking.
- Increasing kubelet eviction threshold is only temporary; it reduces pod churn but risks OOMs. Documented with a follow-up to revert config after stabilization.
- Tweak monitoring scrapes (stop heavy scrape) to reduce control-plane pressure; follow-up to find offending job owner.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups (owner assigned):
- Root cause for calico BPF "File exists" on one node (Jon Park) -> action: collect kernel dmesg, calico version matrix, and file an issue with vendor if reproducing.
- Autoscaler quota exhaustion during bursts (Priya Nair) -> action: work with infra to increase soft limits or pre-warm capacity for predictable windows. Link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-742
- Validate whether recent calico upgrade (2025-10-28) changed BPF cleanup semantics (Maya Lin) -> action: reproduce in staging with stress test.
- Formalize detection alert to include CNI restarts as a signal combined with NodeMemoryPressure (eng-sre-alerts) (Owner: Diego Alvarez)

Evidence & artifacts to attach to PM:
- Prometheus graphs: node memory, kubelet evictions, calico restart count, etcd leader election (see linked artifacts).
- Node logs snapshot (bundled) for nodes i-0a1b2c3d,i-0b2c3d4e,i-0c3d4e5f (S3 link in Jira ticket).
- Calico pod logs for the restart windows (attached in MR 1482).

Temporary notes for on-call replacement:
- If you see NodeMemoryPressure + calico restarts: cordon affected nodes, drain low-priority workloads, restart calico only on 1 node at a time, and check autoscaler quotas immediately.
- Avoid cluster-wide calico rollbacks during an active memory pressure incident unless you have >30m maintenance window and golden nodes available.

Post-incident actions (owners + ETA):
- (Maya) Build a stress test that reproduces BPF map pressure in staging by simulating high pod churn and BPF map creation (ETA 2025-11-18).
- (Priya) Work with cloud infra to add soft-increase in us-west-2 EC2 quota for burst windows or implement pre-provisioning policy (ETA 2025-11-14).
- (Jon) Create reproducible kernel dmesg/log package and open vendor ticket with calico (ETA 2025-11-12).
- (Diego) Update SRE monitor rules to combine NodeMemoryPressure + CNI restart count to reduce noisy pages (ETA 2025-11-09).

Notes to PM: This is a working doc; please migrate to the canonical postmortem template when we have the final timelines and attach the preserved logs. The early owner list above should be reflected in the PM card.

Raw debug snippets (redacted):
- calico: 2025-11-01T02:18:13Z ERR BPF attach failed: bpf: map create failed: file exists
- kubelet: eviction manager: signal: reclaiming memory from pods: freed 4Gi in 3 pods
- etcd: 02:21:46 election timeout, start new election

Appendix: quick checklist for future on-call shifts:
- Where to look first: kubectl get nodes; then kubectl get pods -A; then check calico/kube-proxy logs; then autoscaler logs; then etcd metrics.
- Useful dashboards: "Cluster node health" (dash id: cluster-node-health-usw2), "Network plugin restarts" (dash id: net-plugin-restarts).
- Pager suppression guidance: If the combined alert condition (NodeMemoryPressure + CNI_restarts) resolves within 20m, optionally mark incident as mitigated. If control-plane etcd leader elections occurred >3 times, keep incident open until follow-ups complete.

End of notes. Add any missing logs/commands and convert to final postmortem when we have the S3 bundles and kernel traces.
